messages.text: I’ll read the compact LAr study contract and existing validation rules, then define the paired electron comparison and the limits of any containment claim.

I’m using the repository’s review-validation workflow. The comparison will keep the previous illumination and transport settings fixed, so changes in response, acceptance and containment can be distinguished.

**LAR-COMPACT-PHYSVAL-PROTOCOL** reviewed at **f3ece1d6a6816c8172dfa841d63e5424730e8228**. These are prospective characterization criteria, without a numerical noninferiority threshold.

- **Freeze the comparison:** exact saved 10,000 primaries and IDs; 12 workers; event seeds; FTFP_BERT; 0.7 mm cuts; 5 mm active charged-step cap; ECAL-only, B=0. Preserve services, material and readout representations except explicitly documented candidate changes. Verify complete native readback and configuration hashes. Basis: `docs/validation/lar10k/protocol.md:18–43`.

- **Primary observable:** retain every event, including zeros, in \(R=S/E_{\mathrm{true}}\). Report paired **ΔCV = CV(compact) − CV(old)**, in percentage points, where CV uses sample SD/mean. Accompany it with mean response, quantiles, zeros, low tails and underlying distributions. This spectrum-averaged raw width is **not intrinsic reconstructed energy resolution**. Basis: protocol lines 47–82; `compare.py:121–153`.

- **Controls:** preserve ten |η| bins, ten legacy folded-φ bins, fourteen 5 GeV slices, full φ, signed η and fixed broad regions [0,1.2), [1.2,1.5), [1.5,3]. Label the legacy fold as the **Si–W sector coordinate**, not a LAr symmetry. Add energy slices within the three broad regions to expose energy dependence without confounding it with transition changes.

- **Transition migration:** retain the original common populations—3,999/999/5,002 events—and separately examine the union of old/new partial-depth directions. Provide an old→new geometric path-class table and directional sampling-depth maps. Do not redefine the primary bins or remove poorly contained events. Existing transition limits are explicitly partial-depth geometry estimates: `DES-033:141–151`.

- **Uncertainty:** use 1,000 shared whole-event bootstrap multiplicities across models and projections, preserving their joint covariance and paired contrast covariance. Equal seeds do not make the shower histories identical. Label intervals pointwise and conditional on the saved simulation models. A blanket angular claim needs simultaneous bounds; nonsignificance alone cannot establish “no precision loss.” Report the measured degradation bounds without inventing an acceptance margin.

Two inherited-code adaptations require care: `transport.py:328` hard-codes **43,648** native contexts; candidate expectations must come from its frozen, independently checked inventory. `compare.py:121` rejects all-zero bins; retain them with mean zero, null CV and explicit undefined-bootstrap counts.

**“Enough X0 for 14 TeV pp” remains untested.** The existing **22.639 X0** figure includes the entire isolated package at one direction (`DES-032:216–227`). Separate upstream dead material, sampling depth and downstream material in native angular scans. The 10–80 GeV electron study cannot certify multi-TeV electron/photon containment, hadron/jet performance or pileup suitability. Future tests need agreed incident-energy reach, longitudinal profiles and rear/lateral leakage measurements; shower maximum increases with energy, and average profiles do not determine containment fluctuations. [PDG §34.5, pp. 27–29](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2025/reviews/rpp2025-rev-passage-particles-matter.pdf)

Actual checks: read the supplied mandate, governance, pinned protocol/code/results and relevant DES/ADR records; verified all five supplied input hashes and inspected baseline denominators/statistical definitions. No files changed, fits, native execution or transport.

limitations: Only userMessage and agentMessage text retained; reasoning, tool arguments/results and private state excluded.
Conservative path, credential, email and URL redaction is not a privacy guarantee; review retained text.
Exposed operation counts are per retained turn; journal counts can describe the same invocations and must not be added.
